HER2 patient subtyping in TCGA breast cancer

Claude Code was run in manual mode using Opus 5.5. The PI reviewed all code and analytical choices.

Main results

1. QC and normalization

1.1 Input and normalization

RNA-seq covers 1,212 samples (1,093 primary tumor, 112 adjacent normal, 7 metastasis) and 20,502 genes. The values are TCGA upper-quartile (UQ) scaled RSEM rather than raw counts, so read depth is already scaled out (Figure S1).

Values were rounded, and genes with ≥10 counts in ≥10% of samples were kept (16,453 genes). A blind DESeq2 variance-stabilizing transform (VST) was then applied [1]. DESeq2’s size factors sit near 1, so they change little beyond the UQ scaling. Because the inputs are scaled rather than true counts, VST is an approximate stabilizer here, and later differential expression uses limma on VST values [2]. No sample was an outlier.

1.2 Sources of variation

Across all samples, adjacent normals separate from tumors. ER-negative tumors form a distinct cluster with high basal-marker expression, consistent with the basal-like subtype (Figure 1).

Figure 1. PCA of all samples (VST, top 2,000 variable genes). Left: sample type and, for primary tumors, ER status by IHC. Right: basal score (mean centered VST of KRT5, KRT14, KRT17, FOXC1); normals also score high because of myoepithelial cells.

Within primary tumors, PC1–5 were each regressed on clinical and technical features (adjusted R²) (Figure 2):

  • PC1 (16.6%) is the ER/PR axis (luminal vs. basal), consistent with the TCGA intrinsic subtypes [3].
  • PC2 (7.9%) tracks fraction genome altered and lobular vs. ductal histology, and possibly tumor purity [4, 5].
  • PC3 (4.3%) mixes HER2 biology (ERBB2 copy number, HER2 IHC) with plate.
  • PC4 (3.6%) is mainly plate and processing era. PC5 is weak.

Only PC1–2 are stable across transforms, so only they are interpreted firmly (Table S1).

HER2 IHC has no association with PC1. Its ERBB2 copy-number association (0.10) likely reflects copy losses in basal tumors rather than amplification. HER2+ tumors therefore occur in both ER+ and ER− disease, and clinical HER2+ differs from the HER2-enriched subtype [6]. Global variance alone cannot define HER2+, which motivates the targeted definitions in Step 2.

Figure 2. Variance in each primary-tumor PC explained by clinical and technical features (adjusted R², linear model; negative values shown as 0). Percent variance per PC is shown under each axis label. Era: plates before A213 vs. plate A213 and after.

1.3 Processing batch

Plate effects are mainly a step between two processing eras at plate A213, which is also where adjacent normals stop being sequenced (Figure S2). This is consistent with large plate effects in TCGA RNA-seq [7].

The eras differ in more than processing (Table 1):

  • Normals: 110 of 112 normals are in the earlier era (Table S2).
  • Histology: the later era is much more often lobular (43% vs. 12%), consistent with TCGA’s expanded lobular cohort [4].
  • ERBB2 amplification: the apparent drop (13.5% to 6.6%) disappears within ductal tumors, and copy number is missing for 39% of later tumors.
  • Receptors: ER, PR and HER2 IHC are balanced.

After accounting for biology, plate still explains 0.09 of PC3 and 0.2 of PC4, over half of it era. The share of normals on a plate explains little (Table S3).

Decision: no plate correction (Supplement S4). There are three reasons:

  1. Era is confounded with sample type and histology (Table 1), so correction would remove real biology. Protecting the labels instead would overstate group differences [8].
  2. Correction distorts plates holding few tumors (Table S4).
  3. ER/PR/HER2 signal barely depends on plate (Figure S3, Figure S4).

Replicate-based correction (RUV-III with pseudo-replicates, PRPS) is the principled option for TCGA [7]. If technical replicates run across plates were available, plate correction would be reconsidered.

Downstream handling:

  • Steps 2 and 4: uncorrected VST, with era and histology as sensitivity covariates. Step 2 builds the clinical label from the HER2 IHC score (0/1+/2+/3+) with FISH, allowing a HER2-low group.
  • Step 3: cluster uncorrected VST, then test clusters against plate and era within histology.
  • Step 5: compare tumor and normal within patients (all 112 normals have a matched tumor).

S4. Plate correction test (not applied)

Plate was removed from primary-tumor VST with limma::removeBatchEffect [2] in three ways:

  • All 41 plates.
  • Pooled plates: each plate with <10 tumors was merged into the nearest large plate by processing order.
  • Pooled plates with ER/PR/HER2 protected in the design.

Plate association after correction is ~0 by construction, so it is not shown. The real check is whether biology survives:

  • ER and PR associations with PC1 change little (Figure S3).
  • HER2 IHC on PC3 rises slightly (0.13 to 0.14, or 0.16 when protected), so plate partly masked HER2 signal rather than creating it.
  • Marker genes keep their association with clinical labels, and protecting the labels inflates them, as expected [8] (Figure S4).

Figure S3. Adjusted R² of primary-tumor PC1–5 with ER, PR and HER2 IHC, before and after each plate correction.

Figure S4. Adjusted R² of marker genes (ESR1, PGR, ERBB2, GRB7) with their clinical label, for each plate correction.

Correcting all 41 plates sets each single-sample plate’s tumor to the cohort mean, which erases its biology (Table S4). For example, the ER-negative tumor on plate A26B has low ESR1 (6.2; median 7.1 in ER− vs. 13.3 in ER+ tumors). The 41-plate correction replaces this with the cohort mean (ESR1 11.8), while pooling keeps it at 6.6. The same tumor is HER2 IHC-positive but has low ERBB2 mRNA (ERBB2 11.8 vs. a median of 14.9 in IHC-positive tumors), an RNA/IHC discordance followed up in Step 2.
